findings.title: Path Traversal Open
findings.description: The current implementation is vulnerable to path traversal attacks because it directly uses user-provided input to access files. Using os.path.basename helps to mitigate this, but additional validation is necessary to ensure the filename is not empty or malicious. By adding a simple check, we can prevent potential attacks and ensure the security of the application.
findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.fix_hint: Validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks
findings.fixed_code: filename = os.path.basename(filename); if not filename: return 'Error: Invalid filename'; with open(os.path.join('/var/data', filename), 'r') as f: return f.read()

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted SSH (port 22)
findings.description: The security group allows unrestricted access to port 22, which is a critical vulnerability. To fix this, we need to restrict the ingress rule to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks. By updating the security group resource, we can limit the exposure to only trusted sources.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks

findings.title: Aws Db Instance No Logging
findings.description: The AWS DB instance is missing logging configuration, which can cause important event information to be lost. Enabling logging by setting the enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports parameter allows the instance to export logs to CloudWatch. This fix enables logging for error, general, and slow query logs.
findings.cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.fix_hint: Enable logging for the AWS DB instance by setting the enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports parameter
findings.fixed_code:
resource "aws_db_instance" "app_db" {
  identifier          = "app-db"
  engine              = "mysql"
  instance_class      = "db.t3.micro"
  username            = "admin"
  password            = var.db_password
  publicly_accessible = false
  storage_encrypted   = true
  enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["error", "general", "slowquery"]
}

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: s3:*
findings.description: The current policy allows full S3 access on all buckets, which is a security risk. The fixed policy restricts S3 access to the 'my-app-data' bucket and only allows 'GetObject' and 'PutObject' actions. This reduces the attack surface and follows the principle of least privilege.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the 's3:*' action with specific actions required by the application, such as 's3:GetObject' and 's3:PutObject', and restrict the resource to the specific bucket 'my-app-data'

attack_chains.title: EC2 Public IP and Unrestricted SSH
attack_chains.description: An attacker can gain access to the EC2 instance using the public IP and unrestricted SSH, then escalate privileges and exfiltrate data. This chain requires minimal skill and can lead to critical data loss. The attacker can use the public IP to connect to the instance and then use the unrestricted SSH to gain access.
steps: Step 1: attacker connects to the EC2 instance using the public IP (finding 4333514d in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf)
Step 2: attacker gains access to the instance using unrestricted SSH (finding e63550c3 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf)
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict SSH access to the EC2 instance by updating the security group to only allow access from trusted IP addresses.

attack_chains.title: Path Traversal and S3 Access
attack_chains.description: An attacker can use the path traversal vulnerability to access sensitive data, then use the S3 access to exfiltrate the data. This chain requires moderate skill and can lead to significant data loss. The attacker can use the path traversal to access sensitive files and then use the S3 access to upload the files to S3.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses the path traversal vulnerability to access sensitive data (finding 21d8cf17 in file src/app.py)
Step 2: attacker uses the S3 access to exfiltrate the data (finding e5ee47a9 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf)
attack_chains.remediation: Fix the path traversal vulnerability by updating the code to properly validate user input.
